title: [UI/UX] Recovery Potential Flag — Dependency
walkthroughSteps: Navigate to /claims/CLM-2024-001/overview — the Recovery potential card now asks the Yes/No question directly on the card, no modal

walkthroughSteps.title: Recovery potential
walkthroughSteps.body: Yes/No radios sit on the card itself. Before the Recoveries call this was a modal behind a link labelled "Set", and handlers read it as optional — so it went unanswered and recoverable money left with the closed claim.
walkthroughSteps.expectedAfterClick: Picking No reveals a required reason field; picking Yes enables Save and, once saved, surfaces a Set up recovery case link.

walkthroughSteps.title: Save is a deliberate second click
walkthroughSteps.body: The radios do not commit on selection. This field gates claim closure, so a misclick should be recoverable before it is written to the activity log.
walkthroughSteps.expectedAfterClick: The chip in the card header updates and the activity log records the old and new value.

walkthroughSteps: Answering Yes used to be the end of the trail — the Set up recovery case link pointed at /recoveries, which redirected straight back to Claim Overview. The next three steps are the page that link now opens.

walkthroughSteps.title: The page says why you were sent here
walkthroughSteps.body: CLM-2024-024 is answered Yes with no case on it. Rather than an unexplained empty table, the page repeats the sentence from the overview card and names what to do about it.
walkthroughSteps.expectedAfterClick: Nothing to click — the message disappears on its own once a case exists.

walkthroughSteps.title: Create recovery case
walkthroughSteps.body: Who is being pursued, on what basis, for how much. Saving it writes the two claim-level flags, so the closure checklist row "Recovery case set up" starts passing.
walkthroughSteps.expectedAfterClick: The case appears as In progress and the closure blocker moves on to "Recoveries & deductibles cleared" — one unresolved thing replaces another rather than the claim quietly becoming closable.

walkthroughSteps.title: A claim with recovery under way
walkthroughSteps.body: CLM-2024-003 carries a running subrogation case against the carrier and an already-settled salvage case. Resolving a case as Recovered or Written off is the row menu on the open row.
walkthroughSteps.expectedAfterClick: Once no case is still running the claim reads as settled, not as "no case set up" — the state the two-flag version of this got wrong.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Yes/No radios are on the Claim Overview card, not behind a modal
acceptanceCriteria.plainStatement: The **Recovery potential** card renders **Yes/No radios directly on screen** with a **Save** action. The old Set/Update modal is gone.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Yes with no recovery case routes the handler to the recovery domain

Phase B promoted this from a soft warning to a hard blocker: the fix-it link no longer dead-ends, so blocking on it is resolvable.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Creating a case clears the closure blocker
acceptanceCriteria.plainStatement: **Create recovery case** captures the route, counterparty, section, expected amount and basis. Saving it writes `hasRecoveryCase` and `hasActiveRecovery` back onto the claim, so the state moves `yes-pending` → `yes-active`: the **Recovery case set up** checklist row passes and the **Recoveries & deductibles cleared** row takes over. That hand-off is the point — one unresolved thing replaces another rather than the claim quietly becoming closable while a recovery is still running.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Resolving every case releases the claim
acceptanceCriteria.plainStatement: A case is resolved as **Recovered** (with the amount that actually came back) or **Written off** (with a reason). Once no case is still running, the claim reaches `yes-settled` and nothing recovery-related holds closure any more. **Without this state the loop was unclosable:** resolving the last case flips `hasActiveRecovery` back to false, which under the phase-A two-flag derivation read as `yes-pending` — "no recovery case has been set up" — a blocker demanding work that had already been finished.
